papers.note: Batch 017 manual primary-PDF extraction. Primary PDF methods, results, Tables 1-5, and Figures 1-3 reviewed. The all-player plus U14/U15/U16/U17/U18 layout follows the direct age-category tables. Table 2 supplies all injury, training, match, and incidence rows; Table 3 supplies the most-common severity; Tables 4-5 supply all directly mappable location/type counts. Parent location values (upper limb, trunk, lower limb) and bone total are transparent sums of mutually exclusive source subrows; the Table 4 location rows total 828 rather than the 832 headline injuries, so no attempt was made to reconcile the four-record source discrepancy. The combined hip/groin row is represented only within the transparent lower-limb parent, not forced into hip or groin. Trauma and overuse are entered as acute-sudden and repetitive-gradual because the methods explicitly define them that way. No illnesses, contact/non-contact counts, recurrence counts, days-lost totals, or numerical figure-only values were reported cleanly enough for the applicable fields.

papers.note: Batch 017 manual primary-PDF extraction. Primary PDF methods, results, Tables 1-5, Figures 1-3, and discussion reviewed. This is a one-year prospective Swedish cohort of adolescent female players; the single Total row is retained because the strength/ROM tertiles are multiple unrelated predictor axes, not a defensible outcome population split. The direct outcomes are 71 first substantial knee injuries and 1.36 per 1000 player-hours. The 22 match, 27 training, acute/gradual, and contact/non-contact counts are deliberately not entered because they describe only the 55 telephone-interviewed injuries (16 of 71 lacked those details). Likewise, two ACL and two meniscus injuries are incomplete subtype information and are not promoted to structured cohort totals. No exposure was back-calculated from the reported rate.

papers.note: Batch 017 manual primary-PDF extraction. Primary PDF methods, results, Tables 1-3, and the reported discussion checks reviewed. This secondary analysis of the two-arm cluster-RCT uses Total / Intervention / Control because Table 2 reports pooled diagnosis and days-lost data while Table 1 and Table 3 report the direct arm-level data. No exposure, count, rate, burden, or CI was back-calculated. The Total cells for structured counts are transparent sums of direct arm cells; pooled diagnosis-specific severity values in Table 2 were not forced into broader structured type/location severity fields because no exact source aggregate exists. The combined hip/groin row is retained only in the transparent lower-limb parent, not forced into hip or groin. Table 3 dashes are preserved as blank incidence cells rather than inventing a rate. All outcomes are severe time-loss injuries (absence from training/match ≥28 days).

papers.note: Batch 017 manual primary-PDF extraction. Primary PDF methods, results, Tables 1-4, and Figures 1-3 reviewed. The paper is mixed football/basketball, but Table 2 reports a clean football-only male/female denominator and outcome split; only those football rows are extracted. No basketball data are written. Headline injury counts and all-injury incidence are transparent sums of the directly printed disjoint ACL and lateral-ankle-sprain values sharing each football sex denominator; CIs are not summed. The direct ACL and LAS location rows retain their source incidence proportions and 95% Wilson CIs inline. No player-season, exposure-hour, recurrence, or cost value was derived or copied from the mixed-sport pooled analyses.
